title: Effort Economy Habit Ledger
content:
Purpose:
Quick running scratchpad for my personal KPI system. Trying to keep things small: fewer metrics, fast feedback, lots of micro-experiments. This doc is intentionally messy — notes to self, weekly check-ins, micro-retros, and quick hypotheses I want to try for the next 6 weeks.

Principles (two-line heuristic):
- Marginal gains > new habits: tweak current routines instead of total rewiring.
- Track effort-to-outcome (E/O) ratio, not raw time. Aim to push E down or O up.

Current focus window: 2024-10-28 -> 2024-11-10 (2-week micro-sprint)
Objective (personal): Keep steady output on onboarding docs + 2 small infra experiments while not burning out.
Key results (draft):
- KR1: Ship 3 onboarding docs (draft -> internal review) 
- KR2: Complete runbook for local dev environment (first draft)
- KR3: Deploy and measure latency improvement from batching experiment (baseline -> after)
- KR4: Maintain average weekly focus score >= 6/10 (see scoring below)

Metrics snapshot (this morning):
- Weekly deep-focus hours: 5.5 (target 12)
- Shipped docs this quarter: 4 (goal 8)
- Batching experiment progress: 30% (prototype run on small dataset)
- Focus score last week: 5.2

Effort-to-Outcome scoring (quick system):
- Effort: minutes of focused work (Pomodoro-mapped) + context switches counted as +10m each
- Outcome: discrete deliverable points: doc draft = 3, doc review = 2, PR merged = 5, experiment prototype = 4, measurable perf gain = 6
- E/O ratio = normalized effort (hours) / outcome points. Target < 1.3. Good < 1.0.
Example: last Tuesday 3h focused + 2 switches (20m) => 3.33h effort. Wrote doc draft (3 pts) + small PR review (2 pts) = 5 pts => E/O = 0.67 -> solid day.

Weekly check-in (2024-11-03):
- Wins:
  - Drafted onboarding doc: infra quickstart (3/3 draft progress)
  - Got prototype batching test running locally (small dataset) and saw 12% token cost reduction in one trace
- Misses / Blockers:
  - Deep-focus hours did not materialize. Frequent Slack meetings (4) and ad-hoc syncs ate afternoons.
  - Experimental run wasn't automated; manual steps added 45m overhead each run.
- Quick recovery plan:
  - Block two mornings next week: 9:00-12:00 M/Tu for focus work. No meetings allowed. Put explicit calendar notes.
  - Automate experiment run via small Makefile/script (estimated 2h).
  - Reduce Slack interruptions: set status and reply template for quick triage.

Micro-experiments (ranked):
1) Calendar blocking (2 mornings) + status message; measure deep-focus hours change. Hypothesis: +4h/week. Duration: 2 weeks.
2) Automate experiment run to remove manual steps. Hypothesis: reduces experiment overhead 70%. Duration: 1 sprint.
3) Micro-doc templates (standard front-matter + checklist) to cut drafting time by 30%. Try on next onboarding doc.
4) Two Pomodoro flavors: 25/5 and 50/10. Run A/B on personal days and track outcome points.

Retro notes (quick):
- What worked: shorter deliverable definitions helped me ship small docs. Breaking doc work into 45-minute chunks felt achievable.
- What didn't: optimism bias on meeting load. Need to reserve capacity for unexpected tasks or delegate.
- Weird friction: my 'start-to-ship' latency for docs is often manual review scheduling — need consistent reviewers list. Add reviewers as part of PR template.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Is focus score a vanity metric for me? I need to correlate focus score with outcome points over 6 sprints. If correlation weak, drop it.
- How much context switching is unavoidable given platform meetings? Can I move some updates to async (short slack threads + Loom)?
- When is it worth pushing an infra experiment to Dedicated environment vs keep local tests? Cost/benefit unclear.

Next actions (0-48h):
- Add two morning blocks to calendar and notify the team (15m).
- Write Makefile to run batching experiment end-to-end (2h).
- Create onboarding doc template (30m).
- Ping Ivy and Noah about serving as doc reviewers and whether they'd accept async review windows. (message template below)

Message template to reviewers: "Hey — quick ask: when you have ~20m could you skim the onboarding draft in this doc and leave inline comments? Target: by EOD Wednesday. If it's >20m, mark it and I'll split into smaller pieces. Thanks!"

Behavioral nudges (tiny rituals I want to adopt):
- Pre-day 5-min priorities list on notes app: top 3 goals only.
- After each 90-minute block: 3-min note of outcome and E/O quick calc.
- End-of-week 10-min tidy-up: move half-finished notes into explicit backlog labeled "carry".

Archive / history log (tiny):
- 2024-10-14: experiment concept sketched (batching + prefix cache reuse).
- 2024-10-21: first prototype; lots of manual steps.
- 2024-10-28: started this ledger, set first 2-week sprint goals.

Scratch math (for later recording):
- If batching reduces cost/token by 12% at 100K tokens/day workload, rough monthly saving ~ $X (placeholder). Need real unit cost to calculate.

Notes to self: keep this lean. If it becomes a novel paperwork burden, throw it away and iterate. This doc is a lab: hypothesis -> quick experiment -> data -> decide.

End of ledger snapshot (2024-11-03).
